part.name: Ergonomic mouse-like housing with control wheel
part.description: A streamlined, approximately 102.5 mm long by 65.5 mm wide by 31.9 mm high solid housing with a convex upper deck, sculpted lateral flanks, low front nose, rounded rear heel, lower base surface, rectangular control-wheel recess, and a separate vertically oriented wheel. The STEP model contains two solids: the main housing and the control wheel.
part.symmetry_note: The main housing is approximately bilaterally symmetric about its longitudinal center plane near x=26.9 mm. Small left-right differences and a slight angular offset of the central recess and wheel are present; exact symmetry is not indicated by the B-rep.

Section.name: Upper ergonomic deck
Section.function intent: Provides the principal user-contact surface and supports the hand while positioning the wheel opening near the longitudinal centerline.
Section.physical behavior: Its doubly curved shape spreads hand pressure over a broad area and transfers downward loads into the side flanks, nose, rear heel, and lower body. The opening interrupts the deck locally to provide access to the wheel recess.
Section.geometry: One large freeform B-spline patch with a convex ergonomic crown and an internal opening around the control recess.
Section.location: Upper side of the main housing, extending longitudinally between the front nose and rear heel and laterally between the two side flanks.

major_faces.name: Convex upper deck
major_faces.description: Large upper B-spline surface with two wires, including the boundary of the central control opening.

Section.name: Front nose cap
Section.function intent: Closes the low front end of the housing and provides a smooth leading profile near the control-wheel end.
Section.physical behavior: The curved cap redirects local impact and handling loads into the upper deck, side flanks, and underside while avoiding a sharp leading edge.
Section.geometry: A shallow, transversely curved B-spline end patch concentrated near the positive longitudinal extremity.
Section.location: Low front end of the housing at approximately z=69 to 78 mm.

major_faces.name: Front nose surface
major_faces.description: Low convex B-spline patch closing the front end and joining the deck, flanks, and lower body.

Section.name: Rear palm heel
Section.function intent: Closes the elevated rear portion of the housing and supports the transition beneath the user's palm.
Section.physical behavior: Its broad curvature distributes palm and handling loads around the rear perimeter and into the side flanks and underside without abrupt stiffness changes.
Section.geometry: A broad compound-curved B-spline end patch spanning the rear width and wrapping between the upper and lower surfaces.
Section.location: Rear longitudinal end of the housing at approximately z=-25 to -5.5 mm.

major_faces.name: Rear heel surface
major_faces.description: Compound B-spline patch forming the rounded, relatively tall rear end of the housing.

Section.name: Left lateral flank
Section.function intent: Closes and stiffens the left side of the housing while providing a smooth gripping and perimeter-support surface.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as a deep curved sidewall that carries deck loads toward the underside and resists lateral squeezing and bending of the housing.
Section.geometry: One elongated freeform B-spline patch with outward convexity and rounded transitions at both longitudinal ends.
Section.location: Negative-x side of the main housing.

major_faces.name: Left sculpted sidewall
major_faces.description: Large elongated B-spline flank on the negative-x side, wrapping from the upper perimeter toward the base.

Section.name: Right lateral flank
Section.function intent: Closes and stiffens the right side of the housing and provides the opposing grip surface.
Section.physical behavior: Transfers upper-deck loads into the lower body and resists lateral compression, torsion, and local impacts through its deep curved section.
Section.geometry: One elongated freeform B-spline patch approximately mirroring the left flank.
Section.location: Positive-x side of the main housing.

major_faces.name: Right sculpted sidewall
major_faces.description: Large elongated B-spline flank on the positive-x side, joining the deck and lower perimeter.

Section.name: Lower base surface
Section.function intent: Closes the bottom of the housing and provides the primary downward-facing support region.
Section.physical behavior: Spans between the lateral flanks, carries compressive loads to an external support surface, and stabilizes the housing against rocking and torsional deformation.
Section.geometry: A broad, relatively shallow B-spline underside patch with a near-horizontal central region and blended perimeter curvature.
Section.location: Lowest side of the main housing, near y=2.2 to 3.3 mm through much of its area.

major_faces.name: Underside support surface
major_faces.description: Broad lower B-spline face closing the housing between the two flanks and both end caps.

Section.name: Control-wheel recess
Section.function intent: Provides clearance and positional control for the separate wheel while locally interrupting the upper deck.
Section.physical behavior: The four planar walls define the allowable wheel envelope and resist lateral or longitudinal displacement. The floor closes the recess and can react downward assembly or operating loads. The open top allows the wheel to protrude for user access.
Section.geometry: A slightly tilted rectangular pocket formed by four planar sidewalls and one planar floor; the pocket is open through the upper deck.
Section.location: Near the longitudinal centerline of the upper housing, around x=25 to 30.6 mm and z=43.5 to 59.3 mm.

major_faces.name: Pocket left wall
major_faces.description: Negative-x planar wall of the rectangular wheel recess, with a slight longitudinal tilt.

major_faces.name: Pocket rear wall
major_faces.description: Planar transverse wall at the lower-z end of the wheel recess.

major_faces.name: Pocket right wall
major_faces.description: Positive-x planar wall opposite FACE 0 and approximately parallel to it.

major_faces.name: Pocket front wall
major_faces.description: Planar transverse wall at the higher-z end of the wheel recess.

major_faces.name: Pocket floor
major_faces.description: Horizontal planar bottom of the recess at y=10 mm, adjacent to all four pocket walls.

Section.name: Control wheel
Section.function intent: Provides a finger-operated control interface, nominally intended to rotate about a transverse axis while remaining captured within the central recess.
Section.physical behavior: The rounded toroidal tread provides a smooth contact surface for tangential finger force. The two flat side faces define the wheel width and can provide axial clearance or bearing-interface regions. The surrounding recess limits translation while allowing intended rotation if suitable pivots are added.
Section.geometry: A narrow wheel-like solid composed of two joined toroidal surface patches and two opposed planar circular or near-circular side faces.
Section.location: Centered within and projecting above the control-wheel recess, around x=25.4 to 30.4 mm, y=15.1 to 29.1 mm, and z=44.2 to 58.3 mm.

major_faces.name: Wheel left side face
major_faces.description: Planar negative-x side face of the wheel, bounded by a single closed edge.

major_faces.name: Wheel left tread
major_faces.description: Toroidal tread patch extending from the left side face toward the wheel crown.

major_faces.name: Wheel right tread
major_faces.description: Second toroidal tread patch continuing across the crown toward the right side face.

major_faces.name: Wheel right side face
major_faces.description: Planar positive-x side face of the wheel, bounded by a single closed edge.
